sections.title: PRIMARY DATA
sections._note: Items 1, 2, 3 and 5 of the paper form. Item 4 is the duct section table and follows as its own section, so the numbering here skips 4 rather than renumbering the form. The form's top-right cell — a marked-up drawing extract captioned "(Highlight The Ductwork Which Is Tested)" over a designation such as "SAD" — is carried as the header field `duct_ref`: only the designation is a value, and the marked-up drawing is evidence that belongs in the photo attachment pages (SPEC §12).

rows.description: Pressure Classification * (Class A = Below 501 Pa; Class B = 501~1000 Pa; Class C = 1001~2000 Pa; Class D = 2001~2500 Pa)
rows._note: A dropdown rather than free text: the four classes are fixed by DW/143 and the class chosen sets the test pressure in the next row.

rows.description: Testing Pressure. Remarks: Maximum duct pressure rating of relevant class is adopted as testing pressure, or test at fan S.P. when it is above 2500 Pa.
Maximum permitted leakage = Area x Leakage Factor
rows._note: Entered, not calculated. `formula` on a standard row is not evaluated by the renderer — `calculated` is a dynamic-table column type only (SPEC §12) — and the two inputs live in different sections, which the row-scoped evaluator cannot reach. The engineer reads the area off the duct-section totals line and multiplies by row 3, exactly as on the paper form. Making this computable would need a cross-section formula scope, which is a schema change, not a template one.

columns.label: Section
columns._note: Typed, not auto-numbered: the paper form letters its sections A, B, C, D and `auto_number` produces 1..n.

columns.label: Width and Depth or Diameter
columns._note: Text, not number: the source form is filled "2.6 X 0.35" for rectangular duct and a single figure for round.

rows._note: Photos attach here — the manometer display is the evidence a witness looks for.

rows.description: Reading of Flow Measuring Device, converted
rows._note: The paper form writes the m3/h reading and its L/s equivalent in one row, separated by "=". Two rows here because a standard row carries one value; the conversion is not calculated for the same reason as `max_leakage`.

rows.description: Air flow Leakage Rate (must be less than the maximum permitted leakage)

sections.title: Testing Instruments
sections._note: The paper form fixes three instrument lines (air flow meter, vertical tube manometer, inclined manometer) then repeats Serial No / CAL Date / DUE Date once per meter. A table instead: the same form is used with one meter or two, and this shape is what `link_to_instrument_register` reads so an out-of-calibration instrument is caught (SPEC §5).

An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, and the source form closes page 2 with the instruments block directly above the signatures. Both carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. No `page_break_before` — it shares the instruments page.

signatures._note: The source form draws the second witness block in the right-hand column only, below the first — two witnessing parties, main contractor and consultant/client.
